utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: -- the Cabinet?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You see that it says "Kakanj, the 5th of December, 1995"?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's on the face of the document itself. Therefore, it wasn't produced in Sarajevo, it wasn't produced in the Cabinet. This strikes me illogical that the army commander would authorise travel in relation to an individual soldier.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, may we please have a number, an exhibit number for this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I haven't read the English part of it. It's never come up, really.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please pull this up -- rather, pull it down? Ah, right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Again, Mrs. Vidovic, I'm very sorry to keep bothering you about questions of relevance, but I fail to understand the significance of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is another document that the witness comments on in his statement, in paragraph -- I believe it was paragraph 27. He was shown the document by the OTP. He then proceeds to comment on it. If we look at the heading above the document, one may infer that the General Staff authorised a member of the El Mujahid Detachment to travel abroad, and we've just heard the witness comment on that particular point. And it's very important for me that the witness says what he said, that General Delic did not issue those kinds of authorisations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Are we then to conclude that it was ordinary routine for the 3rd Corps to allow members of the El Mujahid Detachment to leave the country and travel abroad whenever this was requested by a member of the El Mujahid Detachment, but that the General Staff had nothing to do with these permissions? Is that the significance of it?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, no, no, that's not what I said. I said here I'm dealing with the issue of the authenticity of the document, and the part that says the general did not permit or approve, and I did not review the part that has to do with the 3rd Corps, but I would not assert what you have just said, that it was something that was routinely permitted. As far as I'm concerned, I am contesting the authenticity of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I see. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 823.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like for the witness to look at document P1939, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, this is also a document that the Prosecutor showed you, and in paragraph 26 of your statement you said that the signature appears to be -- it was in the group of documents for which you said that the signature seems to be the signature of General Delic. Perhaps we can scroll down the document. It's page 2. I would like you to read this document carefully. I believe you read it earlier, because it was shown to you. And I would just like you to particularly pay attention to the initials here, "FB/FH." According to -- well, this first initial would lead us to conclude that you drafted the document. But first of all, from what I understood, "FH," the person with those initials did not work in the Cabinet. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "FB" are my initials, but "FH," no.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That person or such a person did not work?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, I believe that you read this act, and I would like to ask you: Did you ever see this act before it was shown to you by the Prosecutor or, rather, by his investigator?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on my recollection, and it's been 12 years since then, the first time I saw it was when it was shown to me by the Prosecutor. That was also when I looked at it strictly from the aspect of the signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, I would like to comment now with you on the contents of the document. Could the English version be scrolled down, or actually can we go back to the first page, the first page of the English version, please, and also can you scroll it down so that Their Honours can read it. Witness, please, it says here: "From January 15th, 1995, enable access to prisoner of war camps established in the zone of the responsibility of the 2nd and the 4th Corps, and carry out an assessment of which captured Chetniks can be registered and which cannot."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Please, the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Please, would you agree with me that the B and H Army, in January 1995, especially the 2nd -- and we're talking about the 2nd and the Corps here specifically -- did not have prisoner of war camps?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I know, in my period there were no prisoner of war camps. I didn't know of them, and I never was in any prisoner of war camp. I never went to one. But if you look at this document carefully, it was drafted on the basis of a request by the State Commission, and I believe that this was copied from this request or, rather, from this agreement on access that was taken as the preamble of this act. I state, with full responsibility, that I did not know about prisoner of war camps and that I never went to any prisoner of war camp that was run by the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What I want to ask you is if you drafted this document. Did you draft it and have you ever seen it before?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I do not recall. I could affirm that I did not, specially because of the initials "FH," because that person did not work in the Cabinet and could not process this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you something about the contents, please. It is said here: "Permit access to some prisoners, but not to others." You knew what General Delic's position was in relation to prisoners of war and generally to access to prisoners of war. Please, it's correct, isn't it, that General Delic approved all activities of the International Red Cross and Commissions for the Exchange of Prisoners of War and of humanitarian organisations?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever have any example of General Delic's having a negative attitude or if he ever said, "Do not permit access"?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never attended any meeting at which the general denied access to any prisoner of war camp or to places where prisoners were kept, and I still assert that these were not camps, and I know that when I was the commander of the Operations Group and when we had captured members of the Army of Republika Srpska in Gorazde, that he had ordered me strictly to enable access to all organisations that were in Gorazde, in the place where the prisoners who had been captured during combat actions were held.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, his attitude could not be reconciled with the selective registering of prisoners of war, in your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, if this exhibit -- if this document could be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have a few questions. Sir, do I understand you correctly, you say you didn't draft this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really do not recall ever drafting this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, this document was drafted four days after you took up employment as a Chef de Cabinet of Mr. Delic. Do you know whether there were any other "FB" -- persons by the initials "FB" in that department around about this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Except for me, there was nobody else with the initials "FB" at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you know who "FH" is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have just said that the person with the initials "FH" did not work in the Cabinet, and none of the persons that we mentioned earlier, while I was giving my statement, bears the initials "FH."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you tell us who "FH" is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's no one in the Cabinet and in the part of the Administration for Personnel and Legal Affairs that was on the same floor where the Cabinet was, I also do not recall any person with the initials "FH."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Oh. I thought when you said the person with the initials "FH" did not work in the Cabinet, you meant that he worked somewhere else. That's not what you meant? You meant to say you don't know of an "FH"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no, absolutely, I do not recognise -- or I do not know a person who could have drafted this document and who also bears the initials "FH."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you able to proffer an explanation -- not even an explanation, but -- yeah, just an explanation, from your view, how this document might have come into existence if it was not drafted by you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we scroll down the document a little bit, please. I don't know. The preamble of the document states on the basis of what the document was drafted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. I see it's got a file number, "1/2-29." I notice also that the B/C/S has typed in English "Urgent," not in B/C/S. Would that be a peculiarity that surprises you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Orgent" [phoen] would refer to urgent documents, documents that had to be dispatched urgently, but I really do not recall having drafted this document. I don't remember seeing it in the Cabinet, and I do not recall any person with the initials "FH" who could have processed this document, technically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Madam Vidovic, do you think we have a basis for admitting this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would prefer not to tender the document, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, then the document is not admitted. It's not tendered.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you, Your Honours. I am just going to put -- to try to finish before the break, and maybe before.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would just like to ask the witness the following: Paragraph 31 of your statement, there you commented on excerpts of the war diary of the 3rd Corps. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, you never saw those war diaries before; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You don't know and you cannot tell us anything about the -- whether the contents are true or not?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but if you did read the statement, you will know that I specifically said in the statement that that connection was strange and it was contradictory for somebody from abroad to be given an observation post somewhere. That connection or communication is very strange to me. Secondly, in the military hierarchy, war diaries, reports and other documents are lower-ranking documents than documents of command, so the drafting of those documents were always treated in the same way. So an order, a directive, a plan, is not the same, as well as sketches, reports and other documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You say that the Prosecutor showed you, on page 01851722, an entry stating that General Delic called the post -- called by phone and was connected to the post?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I said, and I said that it was strange for this communication to be carried out, and I remember that there was a special column, "NGS" or something, and then there was an additional note saying "General Delic." That is what I saw in the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In any case, what I want to ask you is that you never arranged such a telephone call yourself?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at all. First of all, I believe that such a telephone call was something that was difficult to actually arrange. Maybe it was by mistake that this connection was put through, something like that perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I would like to ask you just one more question. I put several questions to you about the difficult situation in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and I just want to ask you something. Do you remember the second half of September, 1995? Do you remember that in the second half of September 1995, there was a danger that Bihac and the whole Bihac region might fall and -- might fall, and that the situation in the area of responsibility of the 5th Corps was very difficult, very serious?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the situation in Bihac was difficult from the beginning of the war and from the liberation activities and actions of the 5th Corps also, but I really cannot remember when this was. Was it in the beginning of September, or I don't know whether this relates specifically to early September, because in September, from what I remember, I don't know when in September or October, there were the actions by the 5th Corps when a significant part of this territory was liberated.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just one moment, Witness. I don't know if you understood me. I was asking you about the second half of September, not the first half of September. So we're talking about late September. Isn't it true that you, together with General Delic, in late September 1995 visited the Bihac area and spent time there because the situation there was exceptionally difficult? This is what I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, correct. After the liberation of Bosanski Petrovac, Laniste and Kljuc, units of the 5th Corps were in an exceptionally difficult situation, and staying in the area of the 5th Corps, together with General Delic, I was in Kljuc when the situation was really very difficult, very dramatic, and when some units of the 5th Corps were pushed back and when some units practically suffered huge losses so that they were not fit for combat at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that that was when General Delic spent at least two weeks in the Bihac area in the second half of September 1995?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how long he spent there, but I know that I spent a total of, I think, four days there. I was there for four days, but I went with another team, and then General Delic came and I returned. We didn't come back together, so I cannot really say how long he was there, how long he spent in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So when you got there, General Delic was already there, you found him there, and you left before him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I found General Delic already there, and I left that area before he did. I returned to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, I have no more questions for this witness at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. Mr. Menon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Witness, the first question that I'd like to put to you, it's actually to clarify an answer that you had given to the Defence counsel. And, Your Honours, the question appears at line 21 -- or page 21, line 25 of the transcript. And, sir, the question that was put to you was: "Now, Mr. Buljubasic, now that we're talking about Srebrenica, about the Srebrenica area, the tragedy also affected the following places: Srebrenica, Cerska, Kamenica and Konjevic Polje; is that true, sir?" And you answered: "I'm not quite sure. I think the Srebrenica tragedy affected Srebrenica alone. As for Cerska, Kamenica and Konjevic Polje, most of those had fallen previously into the hands of the Republika Srpska Army." Sir, my question to you is: When you refer to Kamenica, are you referring to the Kamenica which is located in the area around Zavidovici or another Kamenica?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I am speaking about Cerska, Kamenica and Konjevic Polje which are in the broader area of Srebrenica, Zepa and that part down there, not the Kamenica that is near Zavidovici. From what I recall, these are areas that were lost in 1993. The population withdrew to the Srebrenica enclave. So when we're talking about suffering, probably we're thinking about the -- that area and the population in that area. So I'm talking about Kamenica in the area or near Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Now I would ask that the witness be shown Exhibit PT2809.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Sir, you were shown this document during the course of cross-examination, and it refers to the disbandment of the El Mujahedin Detachment. Are you aware of whether the El Mujahedin Detachment was, in actual fact, disbanded pursuant to this order?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I know for sure that immediately before this order, at the time when this order was supposed to be executed, a member of the El Mujahid Detachment had left the Bosnia and Herzegovina area. I don't know the exact number involved, and I don't know if that was the entire detachment, but for sure, some of the El Mujahid Detachment members had left Bosnia and Herzegovina in early January. So I don't know if, in accordance -- if, pursuant to this order, the unit was completely dismantled or not, but I'm sure that in January, a number of the El Mujahid Detachment members had left Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, in the answer that you just gave, you said: "I know for sure that immediately before this order, at the time when this order was supposed to be executed, a member of the El Mujahedin Detachment had left the BiH area." Does that mean that you were aware that this particular order had been created in December 1995, sir?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know about this order, because the order was drafted in Kakanj, but -- this specific order, but I knew that measures had been taken to dismantle the El Mujahid Detachment, and I know for sure that a number of its members, and if I remember correctly this was from the Bihac area, were evacuated. I think that they had gone back to countries of their origin, if I remember correctly. I didn't say one detachment but I said a part of the detachment, meaning a number of members of the detachment. I cannot say this for the entire detachment. I never knew and I don't know now the total number of members of the El Mujahid Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, when you say: "I knew that measures had been taken to dismantle the El Mujahid Detachment," can you tell us, sir, what you -- when you say "measures," what measures are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that it was the duty of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, pursuant to the Dayton Accords, for all sides, and this is stated in the accords, that all foreign armed forces on the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina had to leave the area of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I don't know the exact date that was the deadline. And I know measures were taken at the level of the General Staff, and I know that a part of them left, because I was in touch with and was in charge of checking how these preparations were proceeding and if a number of those people who were supposed to leave had actually left. And this is why I know for sure that a part of them left sometime in January 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And you said, in the last answer that you gave: "I was in touch with and was in charge of checking how these preparations were proceeding." Can you explain what little bit what you mean by "preparations"? What preparations were you involved in?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, I was in Sarajevo. I was not involved in any direct preparations, but this was regulated in the order, meaning that those people should be treated just like other people when a unit is dismantled, that weapons, equipment should be taken back from those people and then for those people to be grouped in one place, and then from that place they should be sent to the countries, from what I can recall, of their origin or, rather, from which they came to the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina during the war. I specifically did not participate in any preparations, and I said that I never was in the area or location where El Mujahid was, and I never knew and I don't know to this date, 12 years after the war, how big the unit was, how many of them there were, or anything like that, or where they came from, all the places they came from to the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: And, sir, in the last answer that you just gave, you referred to weapons, equipment being taken back. Do you know if weapons and equipment were taken back from the El Mujahedin Detachment after that unit was dismantled, sir?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. This order was sent to the 3rd Corps Command. People from the 3rd Corps Command were responsible for implementing this order. I don't think I ever finished reading it. I don't know what's in it, what the substance is. Therefore, those people should know whether they seized any weapons or equipment from anyone, how much exactly, and whether they carried through all the individual items and paragraphs contained in this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. Your Honour, I would ask that this exhibit be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 824.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Would that then be a convenient time to take our break? We'll come back at quarter to 6.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Menon, you said you have no further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had only a small question to put to you. It had to do with the order. At some point in time, Witness, you said -- let me find the place. I'm looking at the transcript. Yes, at some point in time, you told us -- I can't find the right place, but do you remember you telling us that you had not seen this order, or am I wrong, this order on dismantling.

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the El Mujahid Detachment, you mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [In English] Oh, sorry. [Interpretation] Sorry. Would you mind repeating, because I'd forgotten to put my headphones on.

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the order on the dismantling of the El Mujahid Detachment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exactly.

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. This order was written in Kakanj. I didn't see it. The first time I saw it was when I was being proofed for my evidence upon my arrival in The Hague. That was when I saw it. And I saw it today again. I think it was shown on our screens twice. Both the Defence and the OTP wanted me to comment on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Then I fail to understand one thing that you said on page 69, line 16. You said this: "I was not involved directly in preparations, but that was regulated or established in the order," you said. Now, if you did not see this order, what order were you then speaking about?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant this in a more general sense, I think. It was about the provisions of the Dayton Peace Accords which said that all the international armed forces that were in Bosnia-Herzegovina at the time of the conflict should leave Bosnia and Herzegovina. That is the military component of the Dayton Accords. I think it also sets a deadline. I don't know what the deadline is, but I think there is one. I know that right after, certain measures were taken to comply with these provisions or, rather, for members of the El Mujahid Detachment to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Therefore, you were not thinking of this order on dismantling the detachment; you had in mind other orders or rules that were contained in the Dayton Agreement, the Dayton Accords.

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Menon, any questions arising from the Judge's questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, no questions from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That brings us to the conclusion of your testimony, sir. Thank you very much for taking the time to come and testify. You are now excused. You may stand down. And do travel well back home. Once again, thanks.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. President. Pursuant to the Trial Chamber's earlier oral decision, the Prosecution calls PW-9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. I beg your pardon. Apparently we will then need to break for ten minutes for them to sort out what has to be sorted out to hear PW-9. Shall we break and come back at 6.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [The witness entered court].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I confirm that we are in private session. [Trial Chamber and registrar confer].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'd ask that the witness now be shown the document marked PT2849. PT2849.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Witness PW-9, do you see the document on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you recognise, sir, any of the names contained on this document?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise several names.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, which names you recognise and why it is that you recognise those names?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise the name Eshref Hassan [phoen], Abduli Lahkaraci [phoen], Muhamed Momodudja [phoen], Hans Walter Kris [phoen], Muhamed Mualid [phoen]. Those are the names that I recognise.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And why, sir, do you recognise these names? How do you know these people?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were members of the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And, sir, in paragraph 306 of your written statement, when you refer to other members of the El Mujahedin Detachment receiving the Golden Lily, are you referring to these persons?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution would ask that this document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Under seal or --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: There's no need to since this witness's name does not appear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's not there. Okay, fine. PT2849 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 828.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We'd ask that the witness now be shown the document PT2851. PT2851.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Again, sir, I would ask you if you recognise any of the names of individuals contained on this document.

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise one name, Nedal Saleh, the third from the top on the list.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Sir, this document purports to relate to the awarding of the Silver Shield war decoration. Do you know what that is, sir, this Silver Shield?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's also a war decoration, but of lower rank than the Golden Lily.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And, Witness PW-9, again in your statement, your written statement, at paragraph 306, where you make reference to members of the El Mujahedin Detachment receiving the Silver Shield, are you referring to the person Nedal Saleh?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was referring to him, and there were some other Bosnians who had received the Silver Shield.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we'd ask that this document be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 829.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness now be shown PT1828. PT1828.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: PW-9, do you see this document on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you tell -- can you tell the Trial Chamber what this document is, please?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a decision on appointment/promotion to the ranks of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask that we scroll through this eight-page document, one page at a time, and I'd like you to tell us if you recognise any of the names of the individuals who are listed on this document. So perhaps if we could scroll down in the Bosnian version. And when you're done with each page, if you'll just tell us, and we'll turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this page, I recognise the name "Muhamed Basic."

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, who is Muhamed Basic?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muhamed Basic was a member of the El Mujahedin Detachment. Here it says that he was the commander of the 2nd Company, but he actually worked in the social services of the detachment and was just formally appointed as company commander and given a rank.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could we please go to the next page in both the Bosnian and English versions of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These names are not familiar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If we could then -- yes, thank you -- scroll to the bottom.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you recognise any of those names, sir?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If we could please go to the next page in the Bosnian version and in the English version.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They're not familiar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Then scroll down, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not familiar, either.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If we could please go to the next page in the Bosnian version and in the English version. Actually, we need to skip ahead one page in the English version.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not familiar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Before we go to the next page, Your Honours, I would ask that we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These names are not familiar to me.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, sir: Do you know a person by the name of Abdulmelik Basic?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see him right away. Yes, I know the name Basic, Abdulmelik.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How do you know Basic, Abdulmelik?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Abdulmelik Basic was also a member of the detachment. However, his task was not the way it's put here, to be the Assistant Commander of the Company for Morale. Abdulmelik was actually translating or interpreting in the medresa, the religious school for the detachment.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And when you say, sir, "the medresa" or "religious school," in what location was this medresa that you've referred to located?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the barracks of Vatrostalna in Zenica, which was the barracks of the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could we please scroll down to the bottom of the Bosnian language version of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And I would ask you, sir, if you recognise any other names on this page.

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise the name "Nedim Haracic".

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And how do you recognise that name, sir, and how do you know this person?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nedim Haracic was also a member of the detachment, but just like the previous people mentioned, he wasn't the Assistant Commander for Morale of the Company. He worked in the El Mujahedin Detachment's press centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could we please go to page 7, the next page in the Bosnian version, which corresponds to page 12, I believe, of the English version.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The name I recognise here is "Muris Ribo."

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And, again, PW-9, how do you recognise that name or how do you know this person, "Muris Ribo"?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muris Ribo was also a member of the El Mujahedin Detachment. He worked as an interpreter or a translator during religious training for the detachment. He was not actually performing the duties of Assistant Commander for Morale.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And if we could finally go to page 8 of this document and page 13 of the English version, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't recognize any of these names.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, PW-9. The Prosecution would ask that this document be admitted under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence under seal. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number 830 under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness now be shown the document marked PT1732. That's PT1732. And while that document is coming up:

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: PW-9, do you know a person by the name of Delic, Saban?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How do you know that person, sir?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Saban Delic was a member of the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And do you know, sir, when Saban Delic joined the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date when he came.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you see the document on the screen in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the document.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this document is?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order about deployment to new duties in units of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and it refers to Saban Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Ask that the English one be scrolled up, please. Let's see what's written on it.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know, PW-9, if Saban Delic had been a member of another unit before he joined the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know, and I don't know if he was a member of any other unit before.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, or do you have any information about why a document of this type would have been created?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. This is an invitation to speculate. How could the witness know that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, there is information contained in the witness's written statement that perhaps relates to that, and that's why I've put this question. Let me rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: PW-9, do you know or were you ever present at any meetings where the subject matter of persons moving from one unit of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina to another unit of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina was discussed?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was present at such a meeting once.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And can you tell us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before you go on, can we please see the end of the document in English. I would like to -- I can't read the signatory to this document. And, please, every time you show us part of the Bosnian, show us the same part in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: PW-9, when you say you were present at such a meeting once, do you recall the specifics, in terms of who was in attendance, where this meeting was -- and where this meeting was?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a meeting at the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina, a meeting between the Commander of the El Mujahedin Detachment, Abu Maali, and President Izetbegovic. Other than President Izetbegovic and Abu Maali, I was also present at the meeting, as well as Abu Haris, who was the first commander of the El Mujahedin Detachment. Also, Muris Supic was present as well as Sabahudin Albani [phoen]. This was in the second half of October 1994. This meeting was where the transfer of individuals to the -- from other detachments to the El Mujahedin Detachment was discussed.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And do you know, sir, if such transfers had taken place prior to this meeting on October 1994?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before that, members of other units would come and join the El Mujahedin Detachment. However, their status was not settled, or, rather, the units they left would register them as deserters, and that is why their status was not resolved, and that was the reason for the meeting with President Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Now, sir, the meeting that you've discussed, you told us, was in the second half of October 1994, and this document seems to be relating to or dated in April 1994. Can you explain the date on this document in relation to the meeting that you've just told us about?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, objection. The witness did not draft this document, and I cannot see how the witness could explain the connection between this document, the date of the document, and the meeting that took place several months later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, if I may add my little confusion to what Madam Vidovic is asking, the witness said he remembers a meeting and that he attended. He doesn't link that meeting with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The answer, Your Honours, concerning the meeting was in direct response to a question that I put him about the subject matter concerning individuals moving from or transferring from one unit to another, and that's what this document is addressing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's true. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And in response to that, he then told us about a meeting which he said was in the second half of October 1994, and he explained that in great detail. My question to him is if -- or what I'd like to ask him to clarify, if he can, is why he's telling me about a meeting in the second half of October 1994 in response to questions concerning a document from April of 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's just the issue. The meeting that he attended has nothing to do with this document of April 1994. He's just telling you about a meeting that he attended where the transfer of people from one unit to the other within the Army of BiH took place, without claiming that that meeting is related to this. These kind of transfers might have taken place long before he attended the meeting in October. They might have taken place long, again, after he had attended the meeting, but he has not linked this meeting to this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's -- Perhaps that was unclear, but that's precisely what I was trying to ask the witness to do, if he can explain to us why he's telling us about a meeting in October when I had asked him about the issue as it relates to the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection again, Your Honour. The witness is responding to the Prosecutor's question about the meeting, and again that had nothing to do with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me try this:

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Witness, I asked you about the document, and in response you told us about a meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You asked him about -- let's go to the question that you asked, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I think it's on line 13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You said, at line 24, page 93: "PW-9, when you say you were present at such --" I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It's on line 13, Your Honour, on page 93.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Page -- 13. Sorry. "Do you know or were you ever present at any meetings where the subject matter of persons moving from one unit of the army to another unit were discussed?" Any meeting, not this meeting -- not this document. Now, we don't know how many times such meetings took place. He may have attended this -- this meeting is the one that he remembers, without necessarily claiming that it is related to this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'm following.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I've ended. If you're still listening, then you still don't follow me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No, I'll simply move on to a different topic. I don't think I can take this any farther with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I will indeed. I would ask at this point that this document be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document will be marked for identification. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be MFI 831.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Witness PW-9, do you know an individual by the name of Mehmed Jusic?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know Mehmed Husic.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Jusic, Mehmed Jusic.

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know Mehmed Jusic, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How did you know, sir, Mehmed Jusic?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mehmed Jusic was a member of the El Mujahedin Detachment, and that's where I got to know him.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Are you aware, sir, of any time during the course of the war when Mr. Jusic left Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Mehmed Jusic went to Malaysia for medical treatment.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you tell us the circumstances under which Mr. Jusic went for medical treatment?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jusic had a serious injury of the face and eye, and it was the practice in the El Mujahedin Detachment that the wounded who could not properly be treated in Bosnia be treated abroad, and their treatment would be paid for.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Were there any formalities that you're aware of, sir, that were required for such medical treatment abroad?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not perform tasks of that nature, so I'm not really familiar with the formalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask the witness be shown the document marked PT1882.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Sir, do you see the document on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this document is, sir?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time I saw it was when the Prosecutor showed it to me, so I didn't see it before that. It states that this is permission to grant Mehmed Jusic travel to Malaysia for the purpose of medical treatment. I do not see the entire document, the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If we could please -- yes, thank you very much. I would ask if the second page of this document could be shown to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we see the signature part of the -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And perhaps if we could zoom out a little bit on the English version so that we could see the whole page on the English version.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Now, this -- this document, sir, can you tell us which unit was the originating unit of this document?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see it before, I didn't draft the document, but it says that it was drafted in the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And, sir, during the time period you were in that detachment, did you ever see any documents that originated from that unit, from your unit?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did see some documents, but very few.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And do you see the stamp on this document, sir? Perhaps we could zoom in on that.

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, could we zoom in, please.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you recognise that, sir?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not Abu El Maali's signature, definitely not, and this stamp is not familiar. From what I can see -- or from what I know, the army stamps had the number of the unit. This stamp is not familiar to me.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness mentioned the number of his unit's stamp. The interpreter did not get the number.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Would you repeat the number, sir?

utterances.speaker: FERID BULJUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 5689, military unit 5689.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness, other than that, also said a whole sentence that was not recorded in the transcript. He literally said, on page 99, after line 16, he said other than that, the El Mujahid Detachment had a different stamp. That was not recorded in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we get assistance if -- okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I heard it in the French interpretation, I heard what Ms. Vidovic just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Mundis, it's five past 7.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would suggest we adjourn for the evening at this point. We'll return to this tomorrow, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. We'll take the adjournment and come back tomorrow at quarter past 2.00 in the same courtroom, sir. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 15th day of November, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.05 p.m.,
